The §3.5 table now reports a median local recall@15 of 0.667 for the re-anchored operator, a value the benchmark does not produce.

The text now says a two-component refit of 384-dimensional embeddings discards 380 dimensions, when keeping two of 384 leaves 382 discarded.

The abstract now claims re-anchoring lifts local recall@15 to 0.640 (and no longer matches its own 29× factor) when the measured value is 0.543 — the artifact check compares its hard-coded constant to the artifact rather than to the paper, and the presence check still finds "0.543" printed in §3.5, §4.1 and the abstract, so nothing fails.

§1 now states that UMAP relocates previously placed points by 0.41–1.52× the layout width although the measured minimum is 0.31 — the artifact check compares its constant to drift.json, not to the manuscript, and the presence check still finds "0.31" at §3.2 and §3.3.

The §3.5 method now says 500 queries were sampled when the evaluation actually used 50, and no check in the verifier compares the query count against bench/results/reanchor.json, so the false protocol claim is invisible to it.

The ablation table now reports a median recall of 0.527 for the clamp-removed view (implying the clamp changes something, as the prose at line 801 denies) whereas the artifact and the operator row both give 0.567 — the table cells of §3.5 are never parsed, only §B and §C are, and the string "0.567" survives in two other cells so the presence check still passes.

Appendix B now says the scalar form overstates the residual by 1.4×10⁴ at d_esc/‖r‖₂ = 10⁻¹³ when the artifact measures 1.4×10⁵ — the verifier registers that power as the single character "5", and the presence check explicitly skips single-character published strings as unlocatable.

The §3.2 trustworthiness values were computed with k = 15, so the caption now states a neighbourhood size no measurement used, and the verifier checks only the trustworthiness numbers, never the k parameter (the string "15" still survives at every "recall@15" elsewhere).

The §3.5 re-anchoring experiment used 50 queries, so the method now claims a tenfold larger sample behind the 29× factor and the 0.543 recall, and nothing in the verifier reads the query count out of the artifact.

The local-PCA arm refits on the query's 100 nearest neighbours, so the table now describes an arm refitting on 1,000 — changing the baseline the section uses to bound the operator — while the artifact check compares only the recall and cost columns of that row.

The local PCA's 3,749 µs per-query cost exceeds the operator's 16.4 µs by 229×, so the prose now asserts a 19× advantage that contradicts the cost table directly above it, and the presence check passes because the string "229" still appears at lines 125 and 779.

At d_esc/||r|| = 10^-11 the scalar form overestimates the true residual by 1.4×10^3, so Appendix B now reports a 9.1×10^3 error that the committed sweep contradicts, and the verifier's presence check only requires the string "1.4" somewhere in the manuscript, which the adjacent 10^{-5} factor still supplies.

The manuscript now claims the §3.5 re-anchoring instrument averaged over 500 queries when it in fact used 50, so the 0.543 mean, the 29× factor and the 0.981 radial bound are presented as a ten-times-larger sample than was measured — a parameter no artifact check registers.

The §3.1 cost table now states that a prepared-frame `evaluate()` costs 4.46 µs when the committed artifact says 4.66 µs, yet the presence check still passes because the literal string "4.66" occurs elsewhere in the manuscript (§1, §3.1 prose, Appendix A).

The §3.2 table now claims UMAP fitted once and extended by `transform()` relocated already-placed points at one of the seven growth steps, which is false — it is still at all seven — and it slips through because the verifier's published still-step value is the single character "7", which the presence check explicitly skips as unlocatable.

Appendix A's row for d = 8192 now claims the operator costs 6.65× its d = 16 cost when the sweep's own numbers (21.52 µs vs 3.81 µs) give 5.65×, and the mismatch is invisible because the "vs. d = 16" column of that table is never compared against the committed artifact.

The §4.1 summary table now reports the once-fitted global PCA's local recall@15 as 0.156 when the measurement is 0.056, and the presence check cannot catch it because "0.056" still occurs in §1 and in the §3.5 table, so the string survives even though the number it is attached to is wrong.

The §3.1 cost table now reports the prepared per-stimulus evaluation at 4.26 µs when the committed latency artifact measures 4.66 µs, and the verifier misses it because it parses only the appendix B and C tables out of the manuscript while its remaining check on 4.66 is a bare presence test that the four other mentions of that number still satisfy.

The ablation paragraph now states that the re-anchored operator's mean local recall is 0.653 when the measured mean is 0.543, and the verifier misses it because its 0.543 check is a presence check that the ten remaining occurrences of the string still satisfy.

The re-anchoring instrument is now described as averaging over 500 queries when only 50 were sampled, and no verifier check pins the query count because it reads only the chance level out of the reanchor artifact's config.

The trustworthiness column of §3.2 and §3.4 is now attributed to a 5-nearest-neighbour score although it was computed at k = 15, and the verifier never checks the neighbourhood size used for that metric.

The ablation now attributes the recall 0.628 to the screen scale ratio s = 0.35 when the artifact's x_scale_0.25 entry produced it, and the verifier checks only that the five recall scores appear somewhere in the paper, never that they are attached to the correct scale ratios.

Every recall figure in §3.5 was averaged over 50 seeded query chunks, so the manuscript now claims a 10× smaller evaluation sample than the one that produced all of them (the verifier reads reanchor.json only for `chance`, never for the query count).

The committed ablation attributes the 0.628 mean recall to s = 0.25, so the manuscript now pins that measurement to a scale ratio that was never run (the verifier checks only the mean per x_scale_* key, never which s produced which value).

A two-axis refit of the 384-dimensional embedding space discards 384 − 2 = 382 dimensions, so the manuscript now understates the dimensions the local PCA discards by two (no verifier check mentions 382).

The artifact records the re-anchored arm's one-time codebook build at 534 ms, so the §3.5 cost table now understates the most expensive step in it by a third (the verifier compares its own stored string to the artifact and only checks that "534" occurs *somewhere* in the text, which the prose at line 757 still supplies).

d = 384 carries 384/16 = 24× the floating-point work of d = 16, so Appendix A now claims half the arithmetic increase the sweep actually shows (the only published string "24" belongs to an unrelated PCA/project() ratio at line 458, so the presence check stays satisfied).
